Next Steps & Improvements\n\nThese are documented improvement opportunities for future evaluation iterations.\nThey are recorded here alongside the code so they stay visible and actionable.\n\n**Completed in this sprint:** world-aligned request generation (`--world_dir` flag),\n`world_id` on `UserRequest`, `eval_key` on `EvalResult`, standalone `scripts/run_eval.py`\nCLI, 6 new v2 deterministic metrics, 4 new rubric dimensions, paired Wilcoxon test (§9b),\nmetric heatmap (§7b).\n\n---\n\n### 10.1 Fix `ConstraintSatisfactionEngine` preference stubs\n\n**Current behaviour of `_evaluate_preference()`** (`core/constraints.py`):\n- Dining-related keywords (`cuisine`, `dining`, `restaurant`, `food`): binary 0.0 / 1.0 based on whether a matching activity category appears in the itinerary.\n- All other preferences: 0.3 if unmatched, 0.7 if matched (partial credit either way).     "    all_reqs: list[UserRequest],\n",
    "    mode: str,\n",
    "    manual_indices: list[int],\n",
    "    random_n: int,\n",
    ") -> list[UserRequest]:\n",
    "    \"\"\"Select a subset of requests by index or random sampling.\"\"\"\n",
    "    if mode == \"manual\":\n",
    "        return [all_reqs[i] for i in manual_indices if i < len(all_reqs)]\n",
    "    elif mode == \"random\":\n",
    "        return random.sample(all_reqs, min(random_n, len(all_reqs)))\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        raise ValueError(f\"Unknown selection mode: {mode!r}. Use 'manual' or 'random'.\")\n",
    "\n",

    "def load_matching_episodes(episodes_dir: Path, baseline_dir: Path, requests: list[UserRequest]):\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Find pre-existing EpisodeLog files whose request_id matches the selected requests.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Searches both the standard episodes/ directory and baseline_eval/ so you can\n",
    "    evaluate episodes produced by either run_episode.py or run_baseline_eval.py.\n",
    "    If the same episode_id appears in both directories, the last-loaded version wins\n",
    "    (deduplication by episode_id).\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    target_ids = {r.request_id for r in requests}\n",
    "    all_eps = []\n",
    "\n",
    "    for search_dir in [episodes_dir, baseline_dir]:\n",
    "        if not search_dir.exists():\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "        # Both directories use ep_*.json and episode_*.json naming conventions\n",
    "        for pattern in [\"ep_*.json\", \"episode_*.json\"]:\n",
    "            for p in sorted(search_dir.glob(pattern)):\n",
    "                try:\n",
    "                    ep = load_episode(p)\n",
    "                    if ep.request_id in target_ids:\n",
    "                        all_eps.append(ep)\n",
    "                except Exception:\n",
    "                    pass  # Skip unreadable files silently\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Deduplicate: keep the last occurrence of each episode_id\n",
    "    seen = {}\n",
    "    for ep in all_eps:\n",
    "        seen[ep.episode_id] = ep\n",
    "    return list(seen.values())\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "selected_episodes = load_matching_episodes(EPISODES_DIR, BASELINE_DIR, selected_requests)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Found {len(selected_episodes)} matching episode(s) on disk:\")\n",
    "for ep in selected_episodes:\n",
    "    itinerary_status = \"itinerary OK\" if ep.final_itinerary else \"no itinerary\"\n",
    "    print(\n",
    "        f\"  {ep.episode_id}  \"\n",
    "        f\"request={ep.request_id}  \"\n",
    "        f\"success={ep.success}  \"\n",
    "        f\"steps={ep.total_steps}  \"\n",
    "        f\"{itinerary_status}\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "if not selected_episodes:\n",
    "    print(\"No episodes found on disk. Section 4 will run new ones.\")"

    "def run_scripted_episodes(requests, world_seeds):\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Run the deterministic scripted agent for each (request, seed) pair.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Each seed produces an independent world with different hotels, events, and\n",
    "    prices. Running multiple seeds gives mean ± std scores rather than a single\n",
    "    sample, making results more robust to world-generation variance.\n",
    "\n",
    "    The scripted agent is imported from scripts/run_baseline_eval.py at runtime\n",
    "    rather than being a package import, because it is a standalone script.\n",
    "    It calls: get_available_routes → search_hotels → book_hotel →\n",
    "               search_attractions → search_restaurants → search_events → book_event\n",
    "\n",
    "    Produced EpisodeLogs are saved to outputs/episodes/ and returned.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    import importlib.util\n",
    "    from optimized_llm_planning_memory.simulator.adapter import SimulatorAdapter\n",
    "    from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.episode_io import save_episode\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Dynamically load the script so we can call run_scripted_episode()\n",
    "    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\n",
    "        \"run_baseline_eval\",\n",
    "        str(BASE_DIR / \"scripts\" / \"run_baseline_eval.py\"),\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n",
    "    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n",
    "\n",
    "    episodes = []\n",
    "    for seed in world_seeds:\n",
    "        for req in requests:\n",
    "            print(f\"  [{req.request_id}] seed={seed}...\")\n",
    "            try:\n",
    "                # A fresh SimulatorAdapter per episode ensures clean state.\n",
    "                # The seed controls which hotels/events/attractions are generated.\n",
    "                sim = SimulatorAdapter(seed=seed)\n",
    "                ep = mod.run_scripted_episode(req, sim)\n",
    "                save_episode(ep, EPISODES_DIR)\n",
    "                episodes.append(ep)\n",
    "                print(f\"    success={ep.success}  steps={ep.total_steps}\")\n",
    "            except Exception as e:\n",
    "                print(f\"    ERROR: {e}\")\n",
    "    return episodes\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# Multi-seed mode always runs fresh — disk episodes are from an unknown single seed\n",
    "# and cannot be matched to specific seeds in WORLD_SEEDS.\n",
    "# Single-seed mode (len==1) preserves the original disk-load behaviour.\n",
    "if len(WORLD_SEEDS) > 1:\n",
    "    print(f\"Multi-seed mode: running {len(WORLD_SEEDS)} seeds × {len(selected_requests)} request(s)...\")\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    selected_episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, WORLD_SEEDS)\n",
    "elif not selected_episodes:\n",
    "    print(\"No pre-existing episodes found. Running scripted baseline agent...\")\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    selected_episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, WORLD_SEEDS)\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    print(f\"Using {len(selected_episodes)} episode(s) loaded from disk.\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print()\n",
    "print(f\"Ran {len(selected_episodes)} episode(s) total.\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Align episodes with their corresponding UserRequests by request_id.\n",
    "# Multiple episodes sharing the same request_id (different seeds) each pair\n",
    "# with the same UserRequest — correct, since the request is seed-invariant.\n",
    "req_map = {r.request_id: r for r in selected_requests}\n",
    "ep_req_pairs = [\n",
    "    (ep, req_map[ep.request_id])\n",
    "    for ep in selected_episodes\n",
    "    if ep.request_id in req_map\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Ready to evaluate {len(ep_req_pairs)} episode-request pair(s).\")\n",
    "if len(ep_req_pairs) < len(selected_requests):\n",
    "    missing = set(r.request_id for r in selected_requests) - {ep.request_id for ep, _ in ep_req_pairs}\n",
    "    print(f\"WARNING: no episodes found for: {missing}\")"

    "# The manifest records WHO produced WHAT with WHICH config — without it,\n",
    "# you would not be able to tell two runs apart six weeks later.\n",
    "# `config_hash` is set to \"manual\" here because we're outside Hydra;\n",
    "# scripts/run_evaluation.py fills in an actual MD5 of the Hydra config.\n",
    "\n",
    "run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]  # short ID, e.g. \"3fa8c10b\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# episode_source captures HOW episodes were generated (scripted_baseline, react_agent, etc.).\n",
    "# This is distinct from agent_mode, which describes context processing (raw, llm_summary, compressor).\n",
    "episode_source = ep_req_pairs[0][0].agent_mode if ep_req_pairs else \"unknown\"\n",
    "\n",
    "manifest = EvalRunManifest(\n",
    "    run_id=run_id,\n",
    "    created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n",
    "    compressor_type=COMPRESSOR_TYPE,\n",
    "    agent_mode=AGENT_MODE,\n",
    "    episode_source=episode_source,\n",
    "    judge_model_id=str(JUDGE_MODEL_ID or \"none\"),\n",
    "    checkpoint_path=str(CHECKPOINT_PATH) if CHECKPOINT_PATH else None,\n",
    "    config_hash=\"manual\",\n",
    "    metric_version=METRIC_VERSION,\n",
    "    request_ids=[r.request_id for r in selected_requests],\n",
    "    n_episodes=len(eval_results),\n",
    "    deterministic_only=not USE_LLM_JUDGE,\n",
    "    world_seeds=WORLD_SEEDS,\n",
    "    notes=DEVELOPER_NOTES or None,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "run_dir = save_eval_run(manifest, eval_results, EVAL_DIR)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Run ID  : {run_id}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Saved to: {run_dir}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  manifest.json  — metadata\")\n",
    "print(f\"  results.jsonl  — {len(eval_results)} EvalResult record(s)\")"
   ]

   "source": [
    "# Compute mean ± std for every metric across all episodes.\n",
    "# Evaluator.aggregate() returns a flat dict with keys like\n",
    "# \"hard_constraint_ratio_mean\", \"hard_constraint_ratio_std\", etc.\n",
    "agg = evaluator.aggregate(eval_results)\n",
    "\n",
    "mean_rows = {k: v for k, v in agg.items() if k.endswith(\"_mean\")}\n",
    "std_rows  = {k: v for k, v in agg.items() if k.endswith(\"_std\")}\n",
    "\n",
    "df_agg = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"metric\": [k.replace(\"_mean\", \"\") for k in mean_rows],\n",
    "    \"mean\":   list(mean_rows.values()),\n",
    "    \"std\":    [std_rows.get(k.replace(\"_mean\", \"_std\"), 0.0) for k in mean_rows],\n",
    "})\n",
    "df_agg = df_agg.set_index(\"metric\").sort_index()\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Aggregated over {len(eval_results)} episode(s)  \"\n",
    "      f\"[{COMPRESSOR_TYPE} / {AGENT_MODE} / metric_v={METRIC_VERSION}]\")\n",
    "print()\n",
    "display(df_agg.style.format(\"{:.4f}\").bar(subset=[\"mean\"], color=\"steelblue\"))"
   ]

   "source": [
    "# Per-episode table — useful for spotting outliers and understanding variance.\n",
    "# LLM judge scores are prefixed with \"judge_\" to distinguish them from deterministic ones.\n",
    "rows = []\n",
    "for (ep, _), r in zip(ep_req_pairs, eval_results):\n",
    "    row = {\n",
    "        \"world_seed\":    ep.world_seed,\n",
    "        \"episode_id\":    r.episode_id,\n",
    "        \"request_id\":    r.request_id,\n",
    "        \"overall_score\": r.overall_score,\n",
    "        \"metric_ver\":    r.metric_version,  # tag for cross-version comparison safety\n",
    "        **r.deterministic_scores,\n",
    "        **{f\"judge_{k}\": v for k, v in r.llm_judge_scores.items()},\n",
    "    }\n",
    "    rows.append(row)\n",
    "\n",
    "df_episodes = pd.DataFrame(rows)\n",
    "display(df_episodes)"
   ]
  },

    "# Bar chart of mean scores for key metrics.\n",
    "# Skip any metric that isn't in df_episodes (e.g. judge_ metrics when judge is disabled).\n",
    "key_metrics = [\n",

    "\n",
    "if plot_vals:\n",
    "    labels, vals = zip(*plot_vals)\n",
    "    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))\n",
    "    bars = ax.bar(labels, vals, color=\"steelblue\", alpha=0.85, edgecolor=\"white\")\n",
    "    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.1)\n",
    "    ax.set_ylabel(\"Score (0–1, higher is better)\")\n",
    "    ax.set_title(\n",

    "        f\"(n={len(eval_results)}, metric_v={METRIC_VERSION})\"\n",

    "    ax.axhline(0.5, color=\"grey\", linestyle=\"--\", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6)  # 50% reference line\n",

    "    for bar, val in zip(bars, vals):\n",

    "# ── 8d. Constraint-by-constraint diagnosis ────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "# Calls ConstraintSatisfactionEngine directly to surface the explanation string\n",
    "# for every constraint.  This is the fastest way to understand WHY a metric\n",
    "# like hard_constraint_ratio or soft_constraint_score surprised you.\n",
    "#\n",
    "# Also walks through the four logical-consistency sub-checks explicitly so you\n",
    "# can see which one failed — the aggregate score alone doesn't tell you.\n",
    "\n",
    "from datetime import datetime, timedelta\n",
    "from optimized_llm_planning_memory.core.constraints import ConstraintSatisfactionEngine\n",
    "\n",
    "if not ep_req_pairs or not eval_results:\n",
    "    print(\"No episodes loaded. Run Sections 2–6 first.\")\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    ep_diag, req_diag = ep_req_pairs[EPISODE_INDEX]\n",
    "    itinerary = ep_diag.final_itinerary\n",
    "\n",
    "    engine = ConstraintSatisfactionEngine()\n",
    "    all_constraints = list(req_diag.hard_constraints) + list(req_diag.soft_constraints)\n",
    "    csr = engine.evaluate(itinerary, all_constraints)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # ── Constraint breakdown ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "    print(\"CONSTRAINT-BY-CONSTRAINT BREAKDOWN\")\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "\n",
    "    n_hard = len(req_diag.hard_constraints)\n",
    "    for label, group, results in [\n",
    "        (\"HARD\", req_diag.hard_constraints, csr[:n_hard]),\n",
    "        (\"SOFT\", req_diag.soft_constraints, csr[n_hard:]),\n",
    "    ]:\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n{label} CONSTRAINTS:\")\n",
    "        for c, r in zip(group, results):\n",
    "            status = \"PASS\" if r.satisfied else \"FAIL\"\n",
    "            print(f\"  [{status}] {c.constraint_id:<24}  score={r.score:.3f}\")\n",
    "            print(f\"         {r.explanation}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    # ── Logical-consistency sub-checks ────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "    print(\"LOGICAL CONSISTENCY SUB-CHECKS\")\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "\n",
    "    if itinerary is None or not itinerary.days:\n",
    "        print(\"  No itinerary days — score = 0.0\")\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        issues, checks = 0, 0\n",
    "        days = itinerary.days\n",
    "\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Itinerary has {len(days)} day(s): {[d.date for d in days]}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 1: chronological order\n",
    "        dates = [d.date for d in days]\n",
    "        checks += 1\n",
    "        ok1 = dates == sorted(dates)\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Check 1 — dates sorted         : {'PASS' if ok1 else 'FAIL'}\")\n",
    "        if not ok1:\n",
    "            issues += 1\n",
    "            print(f\"    Got: {dates}  Expected: {sorted(dates)}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 2: no duplicate hotel_ids across days\n",
    "        hotel_ids = [d.accommodation.hotel_id for d in days if d.accommodation]\n",
    "        checks += 1\n",
    "        ok2 = len(hotel_ids) == len(set(hotel_ids))\n",
    "        print(f\"  Check 2 — no duplicate hotels  : {'PASS' if ok2 else 'FAIL'}\")\n",
    "        if not ok2:\n",
    "            issues += 1\n",
    "            from collections import Counter\n",
    "            dupes = [hid for hid, cnt in Counter(hotel_ids).items() if cnt > 1]\n",
    "            print(f\"    Duplicate hotel_ids: {dupes}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 3: no overlapping activities within a day\n",
    "        print(f\"  Check 3 — activity overlaps:\")\n",
    "        for day in days:\n",
    "            slots: list[tuple[str, datetime, datetime]] = []\n",
    "            for act in day.activities:\n",
    "                start_raw = getattr(act, \"start_datetime\", None)\n",
    "                dur = getattr(act, \"duration_hours\", None)\n",
    "                if start_raw and dur:\n",
    "                    try:\n",
    "                        start_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(start_raw)\n",
    "                        end_dt   = start_dt + timedelta(hours=float(dur))\n",
    "                        slots.append((act.activity_name, start_dt, end_dt))\n",
    "                    except (ValueError, TypeError):\n",
    "                        pass\n",
    "\n",
    "            if len(slots) <= 1:\n",
    "                print(f\"    {day.date}: only {len(slots)} timed activity — skip\")\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "\n",
    "            checks += 1\n",
    "            sorted_slots = sorted(slots, key=lambda x: x[1])\n",
    "            overlapping_pairs = [\n",
    "                (sorted_slots[i][0], sorted_slots[i + 1][0])\n",
    "                for i in range(len(sorted_slots) - 1)\n",
    "                if sorted_slots[i][2] > sorted_slots[i + 1][1]\n",
    "            ]\n",
    "            ok3 = len(overlapping_pairs) == 0\n",
    "            print(f\"    {day.date}: {'PASS' if ok3 else 'FAIL'} \"\n",
    "                  f\"({len(sorted_slots)} timed slots)\")\n",
    "            if not ok3:\n",
    "                issues += 1\n",
    "                for a, b in overlapping_pairs:\n",
    "                    print(f\"      overlap: {a!r} → {b!r}\")\n",
    "            else:\n",
    "                for name, s, e in sorted_slots:\n",
    "                    print(f\"      {s.strftime('%H:%M')}–{e.strftime('%H:%M')}  {name}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 4: flight arrival ≤ hotel check-in on the same day\n",
    "        flight_checks = 0\n",
    "        for day in days:\n",
    "            if day.accommodation is None:\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            hotel_checkin = getattr(day.accommodation, \"check_in\", None)\n",
    "            for seg in day.transport_segments:\n",
    "                arrival = getattr(seg, \"arrival_datetime\", None)\n",
    "                if hotel_checkin and arrival:\n",
    "                    try:\n",
    "                        arrival_date = arrival[:10]\n",
    "                        flight_checks += 1\n",
    "                        checks += 1\n",
    "                        ok4 = arrival_date <= hotel_checkin\n",
    "                        if not ok4:\n",
    "                            issues += 1\n",
    "                            print(f\"  Check 4 — flight arrives {arrival_date!r} \"\n",
    "                                  f\"after hotel check-in {hotel_checkin!r}: FAIL\")\n",
    "                    except (IndexError, TypeError):\n",
    "                        pass\n",
    "        if flight_checks == 0:\n",
    "            print(f\"  Check 4 — flight/hotel timing  : skip (no flight segments)\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        score = max(0.0, 1.0 - issues / checks) if checks > 0 else 1.0\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Summary: {issues} issue(s) across {checks} check(s) \"\n",
    "              f\"→ logical_consistency = {score:.4f}\")"
   ]

    "def build_comparison_df(eval_dir: Path, manifests: list) -> pd.DataFrame:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Build a one-row-per-run comparison DataFrame.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Loads each run's results.jsonl and computes per-run mean scores.\n",
    "    The `metric_version` column shows whether scores are directly comparable.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    rows = []\n",
    "    for m in manifests:\n",
    "        try:\n",
    "            _, results = load_eval_run(m.run_id, eval_dir)\n",
    "        except Exception:\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "        if not results:\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "\n",
    "        def mean_of(key):\n",
    "            vals = [r.deterministic_scores.get(key, 0.0) for r in results]\n",
    "            return sum(vals) / len(vals)\n",
    "\n",
    "        metric_vers = \", \".join(sorted({r.metric_version for r in results}))\n",
    "        rows.append({\n",
    "            \"run_id\":          m.run_id,\n",
    "            \"timestamp\":       m.created_at[:19],\n",
    "            \"compressor\":      m.compressor_type,\n",
    "            \"agent_mode\":      m.agent_mode,\n",
    "            \"episode_source\":  m.episode_source or \"unknown\",\n",
    "            \"metric_version\":  metric_vers,\n",
    "            \"n_episodes\":      m.n_episodes,\n",
    "            \"overall_mean\":    sum(r.overall_score for r in results) / len(results),\n",
    "            \"hard_con_mean\":   mean_of(\"hard_constraint_ratio\"),\n",
    "            \"soft_con_mean\":   mean_of(\"soft_constraint_score\"),\n",
    "            \"budget_mean\":     mean_of(\"budget_adherence\"),\n",
    "            \"efficiency_mean\": mean_of(\"tool_efficiency\"),\n",
    "            \"det_only\":        m.deterministic_only,\n",
    "            \"notes\":           m.notes or \"\",\n",
    "        })\n",
    "\n",
    "    if not rows:\n",
    "        return pd.DataFrame()\n",
    "    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(\"overall_mean\", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# Compare the 5 most recent runs.\n",
    "# To compare specific runs, filter all_manifests by run_id before passing here.\n",
    "compare_manifests = all_manifests[:5]\n",
    "\n",
    "if compare_manifests:\n",
    "    df_compare = build_comparison_df(EVAL_DIR, compare_manifests)\n",
    "    if df_compare.empty:\n",
    "        print(\"No results loaded — check that results.jsonl files exist in the run directories.\")\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        float_cols = [\"overall_mean\", \"hard_con_mean\", \"soft_con_mean\",\n",
    "                      \"budget_mean\", \"efficiency_mean\"]\n",
    "        display(\n",
    "            df_compare.style\n",
    "            .format({c: \"{:.4f}\" for c in float_cols})\n",
    "            .highlight_max(subset=float_cols, color=\"#c6efce\")  # green = best\n",
    "            .highlight_min(subset=float_cols, color=\"#ffc7ce\")  # red = worst\n",
    "        )\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    print(\"No previous runs to compare.\")"

    "**Fix for group:** Verify `HotelOption.max_guests >= group_size` and check child-friendly\n",
    "flags on activities when `traveler_profile.num_children > 0`.\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.2 Multi-seed averaging\n",
    "\n",
    "The travel world is seeded, meaning a single seed always generates the same hotels,\n",
    "events, and prices. A model that happens to perform well on seed 42 may not generalise.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Fix:** Run each configuration N times (e.g., 5 seeds), aggregate across seeds, and\n",
    "report `mean ± std`. The `EvalRunManifest.world_seeds` field is already a list for this purpose.\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "# Example: run 5 seeds and average\n",
    "all_results = []\n",
    "for seed in [42, 123, 456, 789, 1337]:\n",
    "    episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, world_seed=seed)\n",
    "    results = [evaluator.evaluate_episode(ep, req) for ep, req in zip(episodes, selected_requests)]\n",
    "    all_results.extend(results)\n",
    "agg_multi_seed = evaluator.aggregate(all_results)\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.3 Statistical significance testing\n",
    "\n",
    "For comparing RAW vs COMPRESSOR conditions, a simple mean comparison is not sufficient\n",
    "for a paper claim. Use the **paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test** (non-parametric, suitable\n",
    "for small samples, does not assume normality):\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "from scipy.stats import wilcoxon\n",
    "raw_scores  = [r.overall_score for r in raw_results]\n",
    "comp_scores = [r.overall_score for r in compressor_results]\n",
    "stat, p_value = wilcoxon(raw_scores, comp_scores)\n",
    "print(f\"p-value = {p_value:.4f}  ({'significant' if p_value < 0.05 else 'not significant'} at alpha=0.05)\")\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.4 Token efficiency metrics (metric v2)\n",
    "\n",
    "`EpisodeLog.total_tokens_used` is already recorded but not evaluated. Adding these to\n",
    "`DeterministicEvaluator` as a `v2` metric set would directly measure the compression benefit:\n",
    "\n",
    "| Proposed metric | Formula |\n",
    "|---|---|\n",
    "| `tokens_per_episode` | `total_tokens_used` |\n",
    "| `tokens_per_hard_constraint_satisfied` | `total_tokens_used / (n_satisfied + 1)` |\n",
    "| `compression_ratio` | `compressed_tokens / raw_tokens` (only meaningful for compressor mode) |\n",
    "\n",
    "When adding v2 metrics, increment `METRIC_VERSION` and add an entry to `METRIC_CHANGELOG`\n",
    "in `evaluation/deterministic.py` — the version tag on old results will flag that they\n",
    "are missing these metrics.\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.5 Per-difficulty-bucket analysis\n",
    "\n",
    "Not all requests are equally hard. A useful diagnostic is to segment `df_episodes` by\n",
    "request difficulty:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "def difficulty(req: UserRequest) -> str:\n",
    "    n_hard = len(req.hard_constraints)\n",
    "    budget_tightness = req.budget_usd / 400  # rough cost-per-day estimate\n",
    "    if n_hard >= 4 or budget_tightness < 1.5:\n",
    "        return \"hard\"\n",
    "    elif n_hard >= 3:\n",
    "        return \"medium\"\n",
    "    return \"easy\"\n",
    "\n",
    "df_episodes[\"difficulty\"] = [difficulty(req) for _, req in ep_req_pairs]\n",
    "df_episodes.groupby(\"difficulty\")[[\"hard_constraint_ratio\", \"overall_score\"]].mean()\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.6 Metric version migration\n",
    "\n",
    "When loading older results in Section 9, `build_comparison_df()` already shows the\n",
    "`metric_version` column. A future improvement is to add a `recompute_scores()` helper\n",
    "that re-runs `DeterministicEvaluator` on saved `EpisodeLog` files using the current\n",
    "metric version — upgrading old results without re-running any agents:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "def recompute_scores(run_id, eval_dir, episodes_dir):\n",
    "    manifest, old_results = load_eval_run(run_id, eval_dir)\n",
    "    # reload EpisodeLogs and re-score with current DeterministicEvaluator\n",
    "    ...\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "### 10.7 Ablation runner integration\n",
    "\n",
    "For systematic ablation studies, use `AblationRunner` from `evaluation/ablation.py`\n",
    "instead of running this notebook manually for each configuration:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "from optimized_llm_planning_memory.evaluation.ablation import AblationRunner\n",
    "\n",
    "def generate(overrides: dict):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Run episodes for each config override and return (episodes, requests).\"\"\"\n",
    "    episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, world_seed=WORLD_SEED)\n",
    "    return episodes, selected_requests\n",
    "\n",
    "runner = AblationRunner(evaluator=evaluator, episode_generator=generate)\n",
    "ablation_results = runner.run(axes={\n",
    "    \"compressor_type\": [\"identity\", \"llm\"],\n",
    "    \"agent_mode\":      [\"raw\", \"llm_summary\"],\n",
    "})\n",
    "AblationRunner.print_summary(ablation_results, metric=\"overall_score_mean\")\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "Each `AblationResult` also has an `aggregated_scores` dict you can feed directly into\n",
    "`build_comparison_df()` for the comparison table."
   ]
  }

    "def run_scripted_episodes(requests, world_seeds):\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Run the deterministic scripted agent for each (request, seed) pair.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Each seed produces an independent world with different hotels, events, and\n",
    "    prices. Running multiple seeds gives mean ± std scores rather than a single\n",
    "    sample, making results more robust to world-generation variance.\n",
    "\n",
    "    The scripted agent is imported from scripts/run_baseline_eval.py at runtime\n",
    "    rather than being a package import, because it is a standalone script.\n",
    "    It calls: get_available_routes → search_hotels → book_hotel →\n",
    "               search_attractions → search_restaurants → search_events → book_event\n",
    "\n",
    "    Produced EpisodeLogs are saved to outputs/episodes/ and returned.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    import importlib.util\n",
    "    from optimized_llm_planning_memory.simulator.adapter import SimulatorAdapter\n",
    "    from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.episode_io import save_episode\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Dynamically load the script so we can call run_scripted_episode()\n",
    "    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\n",
    "        \"run_baseline_eval\",\n",
    "        str(BASE_DIR / \"scripts\" / \"run_baseline_eval.py\"),\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n",
    "    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n",
    "\n",
    "    episodes = []\n",
    "    for seed in world_seeds:\n",
    "        for req in requests:\n",
    "            print(f\"  [{req.request_id}] seed={seed}...\")\n",
    "            try:\n",
    "                # A fresh SimulatorAdapter per episode ensures clean state.\n",
    "                # The seed controls which hotels/events/attractions are generated.\n",
    "                sim = SimulatorAdapter(seed=seed)\n",
    "                ep = mod.run_scripted_episode(req, sim)\n",
    "                save_episode(ep, EPISODES_DIR)\n",
    "                episodes.append(ep)\n",
    "                print(f\"    success={ep.success}  steps={ep.total_steps}\")\n",
    "            except Exception as e:\n",
    "                print(f\"    ERROR: {e}\")\n",
    "    return episodes\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# Multi-seed mode always runs fresh — disk episodes are from an unknown single seed\n",
    "# and cannot be matched to specific seeds in WORLD_SEEDS.\n",
    "# Single-seed mode (len==1) preserves the original disk-load behaviour.\n",
    "if len(WORLD_SEEDS) > 1:\n",
    "    print(f\"Multi-seed mode: running {len(WORLD_SEEDS)} seeds × {len(selected_requests)} request(s)...\")\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    selected_episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, WORLD_SEEDS)\n",
    "elif not selected_episodes:\n",
    "    print(\"No pre-existing episodes found. Running scripted baseline agent...\")\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    selected_episodes = run_scripted_episodes(selected_requests, WORLD_SEEDS)\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    print(f\"Using {len(selected_episodes)} episode(s) loaded from disk.\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print()\n",
    "print(f\"Ran {len(selected_episodes)} episode(s) total.\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Align episodes with their corresponding UserRequests by request_id.\n",
    "# Multiple episodes sharing the same request_id (different seeds) each pair\n",
    "# with the same UserRequest — correct, since the request is seed-invariant.\n",
    "req_map = {r.request_id: r for r in selected_requests}\n",
    "ep_req_pairs = [\n",
    "    (ep, req_map[ep.request_id])\n",
    "    for ep in selected_episodes\n",
    "    if ep.request_id in req_map\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Ready to evaluate {len(ep_req_pairs)} episode-request pair(s).\")\n",
    "if len(ep_req_pairs) < len(selected_requests):\n",
    "    missing = set(r.request_id for r in selected_requests) - {ep.request_id for ep, _ in ep_req_pairs}\n",
    "    print(f\"WARNING: no episodes found for: {missing}\")"
   ]

    "## 5. Metric Selector\n",
    "\n",
    "Choose which evaluation layers to run.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Deterministic metrics** (always recommended):\n",
    "\n",
    "| Metric | What it measures |\n",
    "|---|---|\n",
    "| `hard_constraint_ratio` | Fraction of budget / date / hotel-star constraints satisfied |\n",
    "| `soft_constraint_score` | Weighted score for preferences (dining, activities, events) |\n",
    "| `budget_adherence` | 1.0 if within budget; penalised proportionally if over |\n",
    "| `logical_consistency` | Date ordering correct + no duplicate hotel bookings |\n",
    "| `tool_efficiency` | 1 − (redundant calls / total calls) |\n",
    "| `tool_failure_rate` | Fraction of tool calls that errored |\n",
    "| `avg_tool_latency_ms` | Mean time per tool call |\n",
    "| `steps_per_episode` | Total ReAct steps |\n",
    "\n",
    "**LLM judge** (optional, requires API key):\n",
    "\n",
    "Scores the final itinerary on six qualitative rubric dimensions. Each dimension returns\n",
    "a score in [0, 1] **plus a free-text reasoning** stored in `EvalResult.rubric_breakdown`.\n",
    "This is what you drill into in Section 8 when metrics look surprising.\n",
    "\n",
    "Set `DEVELOPER_NOTES` to anything useful — it's stored in the manifest and helps you\n",
    "remember what was different about this run when you look at it six weeks later."

   "source": [
    "# Compute mean ± std for every metric across all episodes.\n",
    "# Evaluator.aggregate() returns a flat dict with keys like\n",
    "# \"hard_constraint_ratio_mean\", \"hard_constraint_ratio_std\", etc.\n",
    "agg = evaluator.aggregate(eval_results)\n",
    "\n",
    "mean_rows = {k: v for k, v in agg.items() if k.endswith(\"_mean\")}\n",
    "std_rows  = {k: v for k, v in agg.items() if k.endswith(\"_std\")}\n",
    "\n",
    "df_agg = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"metric\": [k.replace(\"_mean\", \"\") for k in mean_rows],\n",
    "    \"mean\":   list(mean_rows.values()),\n",
    "    \"std\":    [std_rows.get(k.replace(\"_mean\", \"_std\"), 0.0) for k in mean_rows],\n",
    "})\n",
    "df_agg = df_agg.set_index(\"metric\").sort_index()\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Aggregated over {len(eval_results)} episode(s)  \"\n",
    "      f\"[{COMPRESSOR_TYPE} / {AGENT_MODE} / metric_v={METRIC_VERSION}]\")\n",
    "print()\n",
    "display(df_agg.style.format(\"{:.4f}\").bar(subset=[\"mean\"], color=\"steelblue\"))"
   ]
  },

    "# ── 8d. Constraint-by-constraint diagnosis ────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "# Calls ConstraintSatisfactionEngine directly to surface the explanation string\n",
    "# for every constraint.  This is the fastest way to understand WHY a metric\n",
    "# like hard_constraint_ratio or soft_constraint_score surprised you.\n",
    "#\n",
    "# Also walks through the four logical-consistency sub-checks explicitly so you\n",
    "# can see which one failed — the aggregate score alone doesn't tell you.\n",
    "\n",
    "from datetime import datetime, timedelta\n",
    "from optimized_llm_planning_memory.core.constraints import ConstraintSatisfactionEngine\n",
    "\n",
    "if not ep_req_pairs or not eval_results:\n",
    "    print(\"No episodes loaded. Run Sections 2–6 first.\")\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    ep_diag, req_diag = ep_req_pairs[EPISODE_INDEX]\n",
    "    itinerary = ep_diag.final_itinerary\n",
    "\n",
    "    engine = ConstraintSatisfactionEngine()\n",
    "    all_constraints = list(req_diag.hard_constraints) + list(req_diag.soft_constraints)\n",
    "    csr = engine.evaluate(itinerary, all_constraints)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # ── Constraint breakdown ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "    print(\"CONSTRAINT-BY-CONSTRAINT BREAKDOWN\")\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "\n",
    "    n_hard = len(req_diag.hard_constraints)\n",
    "    for label, group, results in [\n",
    "        (\"HARD\", req_diag.hard_constraints, csr[:n_hard]),\n",
    "        (\"SOFT\", req_diag.soft_constraints, csr[n_hard:]),\n",
    "    ]:\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n{label} CONSTRAINTS:\")\n",
    "        for c, r in zip(group, results):\n",
    "            status = \"PASS\" if r.satisfied else \"FAIL\"\n",
    "            print(f\"  [{status}] {c.constraint_id:<24}  score={r.score:.3f}\")\n",
    "            print(f\"         {r.explanation}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    # ── Logical-consistency sub-checks ────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "    print()\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "    print(\"LOGICAL CONSISTENCY SUB-CHECKS\")\n",
    "    print(\"=\" * 66)\n",
    "\n",
    "    if itinerary is None or not itinerary.days:\n",
    "        print(\"  No itinerary days — score = 0.0\")\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        issues, checks = 0, 0\n",
    "        days = itinerary.days\n",
    "\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Itinerary has {len(days)} day(s): {[d.date for d in days]}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 1: chronological order\n",
    "        dates = [d.date for d in days]\n",
    "        checks += 1\n",
    "        ok1 = dates == sorted(dates)\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Check 1 — dates sorted         : {'PASS' if ok1 else 'FAIL'}\")\n",
    "        if not ok1:\n",
    "            issues += 1\n",
    "            print(f\"    Got: {dates}  Expected: {sorted(dates)}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 2: no duplicate hotel_ids across days\n",
    "        hotel_ids = [d.accommodation.hotel_id for d in days if d.accommodation]\n",
    "        checks += 1\n",
    "        ok2 = len(hotel_ids) == len(set(hotel_ids))\n",
    "        print(f\"  Check 2 — no duplicate hotels  : {'PASS' if ok2 else 'FAIL'}\")\n",
    "        if not ok2:\n",
    "            issues += 1\n",
    "            from collections import Counter\n",
    "            dupes = [hid for hid, cnt in Counter(hotel_ids).items() if cnt > 1]\n",
    "            print(f\"    Duplicate hotel_ids: {dupes}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 3: no overlapping activities within a day\n",
    "        print(f\"  Check 3 — activity overlaps:\")\n",
    "        for day in days:\n",
    "            slots: list[tuple[str, datetime, datetime]] = []\n",
    "            for act in day.activities:\n",
    "                start_raw = getattr(act, \"start_datetime\", None)\n",
    "                dur = getattr(act, \"duration_hours\", None)\n",
    "                if start_raw and dur:\n",
    "                    try:\n",
    "                        start_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(start_raw)\n",
    "                        end_dt   = start_dt + timedelta(hours=float(dur))\n",
    "                        slots.append((act.activity_name, start_dt, end_dt))\n",
    "                    except (ValueError, TypeError):\n",
    "                        pass\n",
    "\n",
    "            if len(slots) <= 1:\n",
    "                print(f\"    {day.date}: only {len(slots)} timed activity — skip\")\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "\n",
    "            checks += 1\n",
    "            sorted_slots = sorted(slots, key=lambda x: x[1])\n",
    "            overlapping_pairs = [\n",
    "                (sorted_slots[i][0], sorted_slots[i + 1][0])\n",
    "                for i in range(len(sorted_slots) - 1)\n",
    "                if sorted_slots[i][2] > sorted_slots[i + 1][1]\n",
    "            ]\n",
    "            ok3 = len(overlapping_pairs) == 0\n",
    "            print(f\"    {day.date}: {'PASS' if ok3 else 'FAIL'} \"\n",
    "                  f\"({len(sorted_slots)} timed slots)\")\n",
    "            if not ok3:\n",
    "                issues += 1\n",
    "                for a, b in overlapping_pairs:\n",
    "                    print(f\"      overlap: {a!r} → {b!r}\")\n",
    "            else:\n",
    "                for name, s, e in sorted_slots:\n",
    "                    print(f\"      {s.strftime('%H:%M')}–{e.strftime('%H:%M')}  {name}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Check 4: flight arrival ≤ hotel check-in on the same day\n",
    "        flight_checks = 0\n",
    "        for day in days:\n",
    "            if day.accommodation is None:\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            hotel_checkin = getattr(day.accommodation, \"check_in\", None)\n",
    "            for seg in day.transport_segments:\n",
    "                arrival = getattr(seg, \"arrival_datetime\", None)\n",
    "                if hotel_checkin and arrival:\n",
    "                    try:\n",
    "                        arrival_date = arrival[:10]\n",
    "                        flight_checks += 1\n",
    "                        checks += 1\n",
    "                        ok4 = arrival_date <= hotel_checkin\n",
    "                        if not ok4:\n",
    "                            issues += 1\n",
    "                            print(f\"  Check 4 — flight arrives {arrival_date!r} \"\n",
    "                                  f\"after hotel check-in {hotel_checkin!r}: FAIL\")\n",
    "                    except (IndexError, TypeError):\n",
    "                        pass\n",
    "        if flight_checks == 0:\n",
    "            print(f\"  Check 4 — flight/hotel timing  : skip (no flight segments)\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        score = max(0.0, 1.0 - issues / checks) if checks > 0 else 1.0\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n  Summary: {issues} issue(s) across {checks} check(s) \"\n",
    "              f\"→ logical_consistency = {score:.4f}\")"
   ]

    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Build a one-row-per-run comparison DataFrame.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Loads each run's results.jsonl and computes per-run mean scores.\n",
    "    The `metric_version` column shows whether scores are directly comparable.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    rows = []\n",
    "    for m in manifests:\n",
    "        try:\n",
    "            _, results = load_eval_run(m.run_id, eval_dir)\n",
    "        except Exception:\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "        if not results:\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "\n",
    "        def mean_of(key):\n",
    "            vals = [r.deterministic_scores.get(key, 0.0) for r in results]\n",
    "            return sum(vals) / len(vals)\n",
    "\n",
    "        metric_vers = \", \".join(sorted({r.metric_version for r in results}))\n",
    "        rows.append({\n",
    "            \"run_id\":          m.run_id,\n",

    "            \"compressor\":      m.compressor_type,\n",
    "            \"agent_mode\":      m.agent_mode,\n",
    "            \"episode_source\":  m.episode_source or \"unknown\",\n",
    "            \"metric_version\":  metric_vers,\n",
    "            \"n_episodes\":      m.n_episodes,\n",
    "            \"overall_mean\":    sum(r.overall_score for r in results) / len(results),\n",
    "            \"hard_con_mean\":   mean_of(\"hard_constraint_ratio\"),\n",
    "            \"soft_con_mean\":   mean_of(\"soft_constraint_score\"),\n",
    "            \"budget_mean\":     mean_of(\"budget_adherence\"),\n",

1	# Evaluation
2	
3	Evaluation runs in two independent layers. Layer 1 (deterministic) is fast, free, and always run. Layer 2 (LLM judge) adds qualitative scoring and requires an API key.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Files
8	
9	| File | Role |
10	|---|---|
11	| `evaluation/evaluator.py` | `Evaluator` — orchestrates both layers, writes results |
12	| `evaluation/deterministic.py` | `DeterministicEvaluator` — 8 rule-based metrics |
13	| `evaluation/llm_judge.py` | `LLMJudge` — 6 rubric dimensions via instructor |
14	| `evaluation/rubrics.py` | `RubricDimension` — structured output schema for LLM judge |
15	| `evaluation/manifest.py` | `EvalRunManifest` — run metadata and result index |
16	| `evaluation/ablation.py` | `AblationRunner` — Cartesian product sweeps |
17	| `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` | Human-readable rubric shown to the LLM judge |
18	| `utils/itinerary_export.py` | `to_itinerary_manifest()` — converts agent-internal `Itinerary` → `ItineraryManifest` for compatibility with the `my-travel-world` evaluation UI |
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Layer 1 — Deterministic Metrics
23	
24	`DeterministicEvaluator.score(episode_log, user_request)` returns a dict of 8 metrics. No LLM calls. Stamped with `METRIC_VERSION = "v1"` on every `EvalResult`.
25	
26	### Metric reference
27	
28	| Metric key | Range | Description |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| `hard_constraint_ratio` | [0, 1] | Fraction of hard constraints satisfied. **Primary success criterion** — double-weighted in the overall score. |
31	| `soft_constraint_score` | [0, 1] | Weighted average satisfaction across soft constraints. 1.0 when no soft constraints exist. |
32	| `budget_adherence` | [0, 1] | 1.0 if total itinerary cost ≤ budget; decreases proportionally if over. |
33	| `logical_consistency` | [0, 1] | 1.0 if: days are sorted chronologically AND no hotel is booked twice. |
34	| `tool_efficiency` | [0, 1] | `1 - redundant_calls / total_calls`. Higher is better. |
35	| `tool_failure_rate` | [0, 1] | `failed_calls / total_calls`. Lower is better. |
36	| `avg_tool_latency_ms` | ≥ 0 | Mean latency per tool call in milliseconds. |
37	| `steps_per_episode` | ≥ 1 | Total ReAct steps taken. |
38	
39	### Critical invariant
40	
41	`DeterministicEvaluator` uses `ConstraintSatisfactionEngine` from `core/constraints.py`. `RewardFunction` uses the **same class**. This guarantees that training reward ≡ evaluation metric for every constraint-based score. Breaking this link (e.g., by adding local logic to either module instead of the engine) invalidates the experiment.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## Layer 2 — LLM Judge
46	
47	`LLMJudge.score(episode_log, user_request)` calls an LLM (default: `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, configured in `configs/eval/default.yaml`) and uses `instructor` to extract structured scores.
48	
49	The judge reads `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` and evaluates the final itinerary on six dimensions:
50	
51	| Dimension key | What it measures |
52	|---|---|
53	| `constraint_adherence` | Were all stated hard and soft constraints respected? |
54	| `itinerary_feasibility` | Can a traveler actually execute this plan (timing, logistics)? |
55	| `preference_alignment` | Does the itinerary reflect the traveler's stated preferences and style? |
56	| `diversity_balance` | Good mix of activity types, neighborhoods, price points? |
57	| `budget_efficiency` | Was the budget used wisely — value for money? |
58	| `overall_quality` | Holistic judgment of the itinerary as a travel plan. |
59	
60	Each dimension returns a score in [0, 1] and a `reasoning` string, stored in `EvalResult.rubric_breakdown`.
61	
62	The judge model is fixed across all conditions for fairness. Do not change `judge_model_id` mid-experiment.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Overall Score
67	
68	```
69	overall = (
70	    2 × hard_constraint_ratio
71	  + soft_constraint_score
72	  + tool_efficiency
73	  + budget_adherence
74	  + logical_consistency
75	  + sum(llm_judge_scores)   # if judge ran
76	) / total_components
77	```
78	
79	Scoring weights are configured in `configs/eval/default.yaml`:
80	
81	```yaml
82	eval:
83	  scoring_weights:
84	    hard_constraint_ratio: 2    # doubled — primary success criterion
85	    soft_constraint_score: 1
86	    tool_efficiency: 1
87	    budget_adherence: 1
88	    logical_consistency: 1
89	    llm_judge_dimensions: 1     # each rubric dimension equally weighted
90	```
91	
92	---
93	
94	## Running Evaluation
95	
96	```bash
97	# All three conditions, deterministic only (no API key needed)
98	python scripts/run_evaluation.py agent=react_baseline_raw      eval.deterministic_only=true
99	python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=llm_prompt         eval.deterministic_only=true
100	python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=identity           eval.deterministic_only=true \
101	    training.resume_from=outputs/checkpoints/final/ppo_model.zip
102	
103	# With LLM judge (requires API key)
104	python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=identity
105	```
106	
107	Results land in `outputs/eval_results/{run_id}/`:
108	- `manifest.json` — `EvalRunManifest`: compressor type, agent mode, metric version, checkpoint path, world seeds, timestamps
109	- `results.jsonl` — one `EvalResult` JSON per line
110	
111	### Load previous results in Python
112	
113	```python
114	from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.episode_io import load_eval_run, list_eval_runs
115	
116	manifests = list_eval_runs("outputs/eval_results/")       # newest first
117	manifest, results = load_eval_run("abc12345", "outputs/eval_results/")
118	```
119	
120	### Converting to `ItineraryManifest` for the travel world UI
121	
122	`EpisodeLog.final_itinerary` uses the agent-internal `Itinerary` model. To display the result in the `my-travel-world` evaluation UI (which expects an `ItineraryManifest`), use the conversion utility:
123	
124	```python
125	from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.itinerary_export import to_itinerary_manifest
126	
127	manifest = to_itinerary_manifest(
128	    itinerary=episode_log.final_itinerary,
129	    request=user_request,
130	    world_id="world-001",
131	    episode_id=episode_log.episode_id,
132	    simulator=sim,   # optional; enables location_id/coordinates lookup
133	)
134	```
135	
136	**Fidelity notes:**
137	- `location_id` and `coordinates` on each `ItineraryItem` require the optional `simulator` argument. Without it they default to `""` and `{"lat": 0.0, "lon": 0.0}`.
138	- `transit_segments` is always empty — the agent does not track explicit transit legs between bookings.
139	- `trip_date_range` is derived from the earliest and latest dates across all days in the itinerary.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Interactive Evaluation Notebook
144	
145	`notebooks/06_evaluation.ipynb` is the primary developer tool for evaluation. Sections:
146	
147	| Section | What to do |
148	|---|---|
149	| 1 Setup | Imports, `JUDGE_MODEL_ID = None` to skip judge |
150	| 2 Request Picker | Load requests from `data/user_requests/test/` |
151	| 3 Model Selector | Set compressor type, checkpoint path, agent mode |
152	| 4 Episode Source | Load saved episodes or run new ones live |
153	| 5 Run Evaluation | Score with progress bar; auto-saves manifest |
154	| 6 Results Table | Mean ± std per metric; bar chart |
155	| 7 Drill-Down | Full trajectory + metric bars for one episode |
156	| 8 Runs Comparison | Side-by-side table of up to 5 recent runs |
157	
158	---
159	
160	## Adding a Deterministic Metric
161	
162	### Step 1 — Implement the scoring logic
163	
164	Open `evaluation/deterministic.py`. Add a private method following the existing pattern:
165	
166	```python
167	def _score_my_metric(
168	    self,
169	    episode_log: EpisodeLog,
170	    user_request: UserRequest,
171	) -> float:
172	    """
173	    Compute my_metric. [0, 1] — higher is better.
174	
175	    Rule: <describe what you measure and how the score is computed>
176	    """
177	    if episode_log.final_itinerary is None:
178	        return 0.0
179	    # ... your scoring logic using episode_log and user_request ...
180	    return score  # float in [0, 1]
181	```
182	
183	If the metric requires constraint evaluation, call `self._engine.evaluate(itinerary, constraints)` — do not re-implement constraint logic locally.
184	
185	### Step 2 — Add it to `score()`
186	
187	```python
188	def score(
189	    self,
190	    episode_log: EpisodeLog,
191	    user_request: UserRequest,
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    ...
194	    return {
195	        "hard_constraint_ratio": ...,
196	        "soft_constraint_score": ...,
197	        # ... existing metrics ...
198	        "my_metric": self._score_my_metric(episode_log, user_request),  # add here
199	    }
200	```
201	
202	### Step 3 — Bump the metric version
203	
204	```python
205	METRIC_VERSION = "v2"   # was "v1"
206	
207	METRIC_CHANGELOG: dict[str, str] = {
208	    "v1": "...",
209	    "v2": "Added my_metric: <description>.",
210	}
211	```
212	
213	Bumping the version stamps new `EvalResult` objects with `"v2"`, allowing old and new results to coexist without confusion.
214	
215	### Step 4 — Add a scoring weight
216	
217	```yaml
218	# configs/eval/default.yaml
219	eval:
220	  scoring_weights:
221	    ...
222	    my_metric: 1       # document the rationale in a comment
223	```
224	
225	### Step 5 — Write a test
226	
227	```python
228	# tests/test_evaluation/test_deterministic.py
229	def test_my_metric_perfect_case(sample_episode_log, sample_user_request):
230	    evaluator = DeterministicEvaluator()
231	    scores = evaluator.score(sample_episode_log, sample_user_request)
232	    assert "my_metric" in scores
233	    assert 0.0 <= scores["my_metric"] <= 1.0
234	
235	def test_my_metric_zero_on_failure(failing_episode_log, sample_user_request):
236	    scores = DeterministicEvaluator().score(failing_episode_log, sample_user_request)
237	    assert scores["my_metric"] == 0.0
238	```
239	
240	---
241	
242	## Adding a Rubric Dimension
243	
244	### Step 1 — Add the dimension to the rubric file
245	
246	Open `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` and add a new `##` section:
247	
248	```markdown
249	## my_dimension (0–1 scale)
250	
251	**What to assess:** <clear description for the judge LLM>
252	
253	**Score 1.0:** <what perfect looks like>
254	**Score 0.5:** <what adequate looks like>
255	**Score 0.0:** <what failure looks like>
256	```
257	
258	The LLM judge reads this file verbatim. Be specific and give concrete examples at each anchor point.
259	
260	### Step 2 — Add the dimension key to `RubricDimension`
261	
262	Open `evaluation/rubrics.py`:
263	
264	```python
265	class RubricDimension(BaseModel):
266	    constraint_adherence: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
267	    itinerary_feasibility: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
268	    preference_alignment: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
269	    diversity_balance: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
270	    budget_efficiency: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
271	    overall_quality: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
272	    my_dimension: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)  # add here
273	
274	    # Also add a reasoning field:
275	    my_dimension_reasoning: str = Field(default="")
276	```
277	
278	### Step 3 — Update the LLM judge prompt
279	
280	Open `evaluation/llm_judge.py`. The judge prompt references the rubric dimensions. Add `my_dimension` to the dimension list in the prompt template so the LLM knows to score it.
281	
282	### Step 4 — Add a scoring weight
283	
284	```yaml
285	# configs/eval/default.yaml
286	eval:
287	  judge_dimensions:
288	    - constraint_adherence
289	    - itinerary_feasibility
290	    - preference_alignment
291	    - diversity_balance
292	    - budget_efficiency
293	    - overall_quality
294	    - my_dimension       # add here
295	```
296	
297	---
298	
299	## Constraint Satisfaction Engine
300	
301	`core/constraints.py` is the single scoring implementation for both training and evaluation. When adding a new `ConstraintCategory`, update **both** the engine **and** add a test in `tests/test_core/test_constraint_engine_unit.py`.
302	
303	### Adding a new constraint category
304	
305	1. Add the enum value to `ConstraintCategory` in `core/models.py`:
306	   ```python
307	   class ConstraintCategory(str, Enum):
308	       BUDGET     = "budget"
309	       DATE       = "date"
310	       DURATION   = "duration"
311	       CITY       = "city"
312	       CUISINE    = "cuisine"    # example new category
313	       ...
314	   ```
315	
316	2. Add an `_evaluate_cuisine()` method in `ConstraintSatisfactionEngine`:
317	   ```python
318	   def _evaluate_cuisine(
319	       self, itinerary: Itinerary, constraint: Constraint
320	   ) -> ConstraintSatisfactionResult:
321	       # constraint.value is the required cuisine string
322	       # check if any restaurant booking matches
323	       ...
324	   ```
325	
326	3. Wire it into the `_evaluate_single()` dispatcher:
327	   ```python
328	   elif constraint.category == ConstraintCategory.CUISINE:
329	       return self._evaluate_cuisine(itinerary, constraint)
330	   ```
331	
332	4. Add unit tests in `tests/test_core/test_constraint_engine_unit.py`.
333	
334	---
335	
336	## Ablation Studies
337	
338	`AblationRunner` in `evaluation/ablation.py` sweeps a Cartesian product of config axes:
339	
340	```python
341	from optimized_llm_planning_memory.evaluation.ablation import AblationRunner
342	
343	runner = AblationRunner(
344	    axes={
345	        "agent.mode":            ["raw", "llm_summary", "compressor"],
346	        "compressor.type":       ["identity", "transformer"],
347	        "training.num_timesteps": [50_000, 200_000],
348	    },
349	    base_config=base_config,
350	    n_episodes_per_cell=10,
351	)
352	results = runner.run()     # dict[condition_key → list[EvalResult]]
353	runner.report(results)     # prints mean ± std table
354	```
355	
356	See `notebooks/06_evaluation.ipynb` Section 8 for an interactive wiring example.
357	
358	---
359	
360	## Metric Versioning
361	
362	Every `EvalResult` is stamped with `METRIC_VERSION`. When the metric schema changes:
363	- Old results retain their original version tag.
364	- The `runs_comparison` notebook section detects version mismatches and flags them rather than silently averaging incompatible numbers.
365	- Never remove a version from `METRIC_CHANGELOG` — it's the audit trail.
366

# Evaluation

Evaluation runs in two independent layers. Layer 1 (deterministic) is fast, free, and always run. Layer 2 (LLM judge) adds qualitative scoring and requires an API key.

---

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `evaluation/evaluator.py` | `Evaluator` — orchestrates both layers, writes results |
| `evaluation/deterministic.py` | `DeterministicEvaluator` — 8 rule-based metrics |
| `evaluation/llm_judge.py` | `LLMJudge` — 6 rubric dimensions via instructor |
| `evaluation/rubrics.py` | `RubricDimension` — structured output schema for LLM judge |
| `evaluation/manifest.py` | `EvalRunManifest` — run metadata and result index |
| `evaluation/ablation.py` | `AblationRunner` — Cartesian product sweeps |
| `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` | Human-readable rubric shown to the LLM judge |
| `utils/itinerary_export.py` | `to_itinerary_manifest()` — converts agent-internal `Itinerary` → `ItineraryManifest` for compatibility with the `my-travel-world` evaluation UI |

---

## Layer 1 — Deterministic Metrics

`DeterministicEvaluator.score(episode_log, user_request)` returns a dict of 8 metrics. No LLM calls. Stamped with `METRIC_VERSION = "v1"` on every `EvalResult`.

### Metric reference

| Metric key | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hard_constraint_ratio` | [0, 1] | Fraction of hard constraints satisfied. **Primary success criterion** — double-weighted in the overall score. |
| `soft_constraint_score` | [0, 1] | Weighted average satisfaction across soft constraints. 1.0 when no soft constraints exist. |
| `budget_adherence` | [0, 1] | 1.0 if total itinerary cost ≤ budget; decreases proportionally if over. |
| `logical_consistency` | [0, 1] | 1.0 if: days are sorted chronologically AND no hotel is booked twice. |
| `tool_efficiency` | [0, 1] | `1 - redundant_calls / total_calls`. Higher is better. |
| `tool_failure_rate` | [0, 1] | `failed_calls / total_calls`. Lower is better. |
| `avg_tool_latency_ms` | ≥ 0 | Mean latency per tool call in milliseconds. |
| `steps_per_episode` | ≥ 1 | Total ReAct steps taken. |

### Critical invariant

`DeterministicEvaluator` uses `ConstraintSatisfactionEngine` from `core/constraints.py`. `RewardFunction` uses the **same class**. This guarantees that training reward ≡ evaluation metric for every constraint-based score. Breaking this link (e.g., by adding local logic to either module instead of the engine) invalidates the experiment.

---

## Layer 2 — LLM Judge

`LLMJudge.score(episode_log, user_request)` calls an LLM (default: `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, configured in `configs/eval/default.yaml`) and uses `instructor` to extract structured scores.

The judge reads `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` and evaluates the final itinerary on six dimensions:

| Dimension key | What it measures |
|---|---|
| `constraint_adherence` | Were all stated hard and soft constraints respected? |
| `itinerary_feasibility` | Can a traveler actually execute this plan (timing, logistics)? |
| `preference_alignment` | Does the itinerary reflect the traveler's stated preferences and style? |
| `diversity_balance` | Good mix of activity types, neighborhoods, price points? |
| `budget_efficiency` | Was the budget used wisely — value for money? |
| `overall_quality` | Holistic judgment of the itinerary as a travel plan. |

Each dimension returns a score in [0, 1] and a `reasoning` string, stored in `EvalResult.rubric_breakdown`.

The judge model is fixed across all conditions for fairness. Do not change `judge_model_id` mid-experiment.

---

## Overall Score

```
overall = (
    2 × hard_constraint_ratio
  + soft_constraint_score
  + tool_efficiency
  + budget_adherence
  + logical_consistency
  + sum(llm_judge_scores)   # if judge ran
) / total_components
```

Scoring weights are configured in `configs/eval/default.yaml`:

```yaml
eval:
  scoring_weights:
    hard_constraint_ratio: 2    # doubled — primary success criterion
    soft_constraint_score: 1
    tool_efficiency: 1
    budget_adherence: 1
    logical_consistency: 1
    llm_judge_dimensions: 1     # each rubric dimension equally weighted
```

---

## Running Evaluation

```bash
# All three conditions, deterministic only (no API key needed)
python scripts/run_evaluation.py agent=react_baseline_raw      eval.deterministic_only=true
python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=llm_prompt         eval.deterministic_only=true
python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=identity           eval.deterministic_only=true \
    training.resume_from=outputs/checkpoints/final/ppo_model.zip

# With LLM judge (requires API key)
python scripts/run_evaluation.py compressor=identity
```

Results land in `outputs/eval_results/{run_id}/`:
- `manifest.json` — `EvalRunManifest`: compressor type, agent mode, metric version, checkpoint path, world seeds, timestamps
- `results.jsonl` — one `EvalResult` JSON per line

### Load previous results in Python

```python
from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.episode_io import load_eval_run, list_eval_runs

manifests = list_eval_runs("outputs/eval_results/")       # newest first
manifest, results = load_eval_run("abc12345", "outputs/eval_results/")
```

### Converting to `ItineraryManifest` for the travel world UI

`EpisodeLog.final_itinerary` uses the agent-internal `Itinerary` model. To display the result in the `my-travel-world` evaluation UI (which expects an `ItineraryManifest`), use the conversion utility:

```python
from optimized_llm_planning_memory.utils.itinerary_export import to_itinerary_manifest

manifest = to_itinerary_manifest(
    itinerary=episode_log.final_itinerary,
    request=user_request,
    world_id="world-001",
    episode_id=episode_log.episode_id,
    simulator=sim,   # optional; enables location_id/coordinates lookup
)
```

**Fidelity notes:**
- `location_id` and `coordinates` on each `ItineraryItem` require the optional `simulator` argument. Without it they default to `""` and `{"lat": 0.0, "lon": 0.0}`.
- `transit_segments` is always empty — the agent does not track explicit transit legs between bookings.
- `trip_date_range` is derived from the earliest and latest dates across all days in the itinerary.

---

## Interactive Evaluation Notebook

`notebooks/06_evaluation.ipynb` is the primary developer tool for evaluation. Sections:

| Section | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 Setup | Imports, `JUDGE_MODEL_ID = None` to skip judge |
| 2 Request Picker | Load requests from `data/user_requests/test/` |
| 3 Model Selector | Set compressor type, checkpoint path, agent mode |
| 4 Episode Source | Load saved episodes or run new ones live |
| 5 Run Evaluation | Score with progress bar; auto-saves manifest |
| 6 Results Table | Mean ± std per metric; bar chart |
| 7 Drill-Down | Full trajectory + metric bars for one episode |
| 8 Runs Comparison | Side-by-side table of up to 5 recent runs |

---

## Adding a Deterministic Metric

### Step 1 — Implement the scoring logic

Open `evaluation/deterministic.py`. Add a private method following the existing pattern:

```python
def _score_my_metric(
    self,
    episode_log: EpisodeLog,
    user_request: UserRequest,
) -> float:
    """
    Compute my_metric. [0, 1] — higher is better.

    Rule: <describe what you measure and how the score is computed>
    """
    if episode_log.final_itinerary is None:
        return 0.0
    # ... your scoring logic using episode_log and user_request ...
    return score  # float in [0, 1]
```

If the metric requires constraint evaluation, call `self._engine.evaluate(itinerary, constraints)` — do not re-implement constraint logic locally.

### Step 2 — Add it to `score()`

```python
def score(
    self,
    episode_log: EpisodeLog,
    user_request: UserRequest,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ...
    return {
        "hard_constraint_ratio": ...,
        "soft_constraint_score": ...,
        # ... existing metrics ...
        "my_metric": self._score_my_metric(episode_log, user_request),  # add here
    }
```

### Step 3 — Bump the metric version

```python
METRIC_VERSION = "v2"   # was "v1"

METRIC_CHANGELOG: dict[str, str] = {
    "v1": "...",
    "v2": "Added my_metric: <description>.",
}
```

Bumping the version stamps new `EvalResult` objects with `"v2"`, allowing old and new results to coexist without confusion.

### Step 4 — Add a scoring weight

```yaml
# configs/eval/default.yaml
eval:
  scoring_weights:
    ...
    my_metric: 1       # document the rationale in a comment
```

### Step 5 — Write a test

```python
# tests/test_evaluation/test_deterministic.py
def test_my_metric_perfect_case(sample_episode_log, sample_user_request):
    evaluator = DeterministicEvaluator()
    scores = evaluator.score(sample_episode_log, sample_user_request)
    assert "my_metric" in scores
    assert 0.0 <= scores["my_metric"] <= 1.0

def test_my_metric_zero_on_failure(failing_episode_log, sample_user_request):
    scores = DeterministicEvaluator().score(failing_episode_log, sample_user_request)
    assert scores["my_metric"] == 0.0
```

---

## Adding a Rubric Dimension

### Step 1 — Add the dimension to the rubric file

Open `data/rubrics/itinerary_rubric_v1.md` and add a new `##` section:

```markdown
## my_dimension (0–1 scale)

**What to assess:** <clear description for the judge LLM>

**Score 1.0:** <what perfect looks like>
**Score 0.5:** <what adequate looks like>
**Score 0.0:** <what failure looks like>
```

The LLM judge reads this file verbatim. Be specific and give concrete examples at each anchor point.

### Step 2 — Add the dimension key to `RubricDimension`

Open `evaluation/rubrics.py`:

```python
class RubricDimension(BaseModel):
    constraint_adherence: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    itinerary_feasibility: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    preference_alignment: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    diversity_balance: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    budget_efficiency: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    overall_quality: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    my_dimension: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)  # add here

    # Also add a reasoning field:
    my_dimension_reasoning: str = Field(default="")
```

### Step 3 — Update the LLM judge prompt

Open `evaluation/llm_judge.py`. The judge prompt references the rubric dimensions. Add `my_dimension` to the dimension list in the prompt template so the LLM knows to score it.

### Step 4 — Add a scoring weight

```yaml
# configs/eval/default.yaml
eval:
  judge_dimensions:
    - constraint_adherence
    - itinerary_feasibility
    - preference_alignment
    - diversity_balance
    - budget_efficiency
    - overall_quality
    - my_dimension       # add here
```

---

## Constraint Satisfaction Engine

`core/constraints.py` is the single scoring implementation for both training and evaluation. When adding a new `ConstraintCategory`, update **both** the engine **and** add a test in `tests/test_core/test_constraint_engine_unit.py`.

### Adding a new constraint category

1. Add the enum value to `ConstraintCategory` in `core/models.py`:
   ```python
   class ConstraintCategory(str, Enum):
       BUDGET     = "budget"
       DATE       = "date"
       DURATION   = "duration"
       CITY       = "city"
       CUISINE    = "cuisine"    # example new category
       ...
   ```

2. Add an `_evaluate_cuisine()` method in `ConstraintSatisfactionEngine`:
   ```python
   def _evaluate_cuisine(
       self, itinerary: Itinerary, constraint: Constraint
   ) -> ConstraintSatisfactionResult:
       # constraint.value is the required cuisine string
       # check if any restaurant booking matches
       ...
   ```

3. Wire it into the `_evaluate_single()` dispatcher:
   ```python
   elif constraint.category == ConstraintCategory.CUISINE:
       return self._evaluate_cuisine(itinerary, constraint)
   ```

4. Add unit tests in `tests/test_core/test_constraint_engine_unit.py`.

## Ablation Studies

`AblationRunner` in `evaluation/ablation.py` sweeps a Cartesian product of config axes:

```python
from optimized_llm_planning_memory.evaluation.ablation import AblationRunner

runner = AblationRunner(
    axes={
        "agent.mode":            ["raw", "llm_summary", "compressor"],
        "compressor.type":       ["identity", "transformer"],
        "training.num_timesteps": [50_000, 200_000],
    },
    base_config=base_config,
    n_episodes_per_cell=10,
)
results = runner.run()     # dict[condition_key → list[EvalResult]]
runner.report(results)     # prints mean ± std table
```

See `notebooks/06_evaluation.ipynb` Section 8 for an interactive wiring example.

## Metric Versioning

Every `EvalResult` is stamped with `METRIC_VERSION`. When the metric schema changes:
- Old results retain their original version tag.
- The `runs_comparison` notebook section detects version mismatches and flags them rather than silently averaging incompatible numbers.
- Never remove a version from `METRIC_CHANGELOG` — it's the audit trail.

7	## What This Is
8	
9	This repository investigates whether **context compression alone** — without fine-tuning the planning LLM — can outperform raw and summarized ReAct trajectories for constraint-satisfying travel planning.
10	
11	A trainable **compressor** distills a growing ReAct agent trajectory into a compact structured text state. That state is injected into the agent's context window at each compression event. The compressor is trained end-to-end via **Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)**, with rewards shaped by hard/soft constraint satisfaction, tool efficiency, and logical consistency.
12	
13	Three experimental conditions are compared:
14	
15	| Condition | Config | Description |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| **RAW** | `agent=react_baseline_raw` | Full trajectory appended verbatim — no compression |
18	| **LLM Summary** | `agent=react_default compressor=llm_prompt` | Separate LLM call summarizes trajectory at each step |

# Optimized LLM Planning with Memory

**Columbia MSDS — STATGR5293: Generative AI with LLMs — Final Project (Spring 2026)**

---

## What This Is

This repository investigates whether **context compression alone** — without fine-tuning the planning LLM — can outperform raw and summarized ReAct trajectories for constraint-satisfying travel planning.

A trainable **compressor** distills a growing ReAct agent trajectory into a compact structured text state. That state is injected into the agent's context window at each compression event. The compressor is trained end-to-end via **Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)**, with rewards shaped by hard/soft constraint satisfaction, tool efficiency, and logical consistency.

Three experimental conditions are compared:

| Condition | Config | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **RAW** | `agent=react_baseline_raw` | Full trajectory appended verbatim — no compression |
| **LLM Summary** | `agent=react_default compressor=llm_prompt` | Separate LLM call summarizes trajectory at each step |
| **Trained Compressor** | `agent=react_default compressor=identity` or `transformer` | PPO-trained compressor produces a structured 6-section memory state |

---

## Architecture

```
UserRequest
    │
    ▼
ReActAgent  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    think → act → observe loop                                        │
    │                                                                 │
    ├─► ContextBuilder    (RAW | LLM_SUMMARY | COMPRESSOR mode)      │
    │       builds the LLM prompt from:                              │
    │       [SYSTEM] + [USER REQUEST] + [CURRENT ITINERARY STATE]   │
    │       + [MEMORY] + [TOOL SCHEMA] + [FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES]        │
    │                                                                 │
    ├─► ToolRegistry ──► BaseTool ──► SimulatorAdapter               │
    │       middleware       Template Method   wraps travel_world     │
    │       (validation, tracking, events, error feedback)           │
    │                                                                 │
    └─► Compressor  (CompressorBase ABC)                             │
            every N steps or on token threshold                       │
            trajectory → CompressedState (6 required sections)       │
                                                                      │
EpisodeLog ◄──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    │   frozen data contract: trajectory, compressed_states,
    │   final_itinerary, reward_components, tool_stats, termination_reason
    │
    ├─► RewardFunction            (PPO training signal)
    │       uses ConstraintSatisfactionEngine
    │
    └─► Evaluator
            DeterministicEvaluator   (8 metrics, no LLM)
            LLMJudge                 (6 rubric dimensions)
```

### Critical Design Invariants

1. **`ConstraintSatisfactionEngine`** (`core/constraints.py`) is the **single implementation** imported by both `RewardFunction` and `DeterministicEvaluator`. Training signal ≡ evaluation metric — by construction.
2. **`EpisodeLog`** is the universal data contract. Nothing downstream reads `Trajectory` directly.
3. **`CompressedStateTemplate`** enforces a fixed 6-section output schema, preventing the compressor from drifting toward unstructured actions.
4. **`SimulatorProtocol`** uses `typing.Protocol` structural typing so the external simulator never imports from this codebase.

---

## Module Map

| Module | Purpose | Deep-dive |
